🫘 When to plant cowpea (beans) in Nigeria

Also called Ẹ̀wà (Yoruba), Wake (Hausa) and Agwa (Igbo).

Quick answer: Plant cowpea (beans) in Nigeria from July to September and harvest from September to November. North: sown July–August so pods dry after the rains. South: sown August–September as a late-season crop.

PlantJuly to September
HarvestSeptember to November
Grows inAll regions
TypeLegumes & oilseeds
Local namesẸ̀wà · Wake · Agwa

About cowpea (beans)

Nigeria is the world's largest producer and consumer of cowpea. In 2019 Nigeria approved a pod-borer-resistant (PBR) cowpea variety.

How to plant cowpea (beans) well

Store dry beans in hermetic triple-layer (PICS) bags to stop weevils without chemicals.

North: sown July–August so pods dry after the rains. South: sown August–September as a late-season crop.

Diseases and pests of cowpea (beans)

  • Maruca pod borer & flower thrips (pests)Spray recommended insecticide at flowering and podding, or grow PBR cowpea.
  • Cowpea aphid-borne mosaic virusUse resistant varieties and clean seed; control aphids early.

Questions farmers ask

When is the best time to plant cowpea (beans) in Nigeria?

Plant cowpea (beans) in Nigeria from July to September and harvest from September to November. North: sown July–August so pods dry after the rains. South: sown August–September as a late-season crop.

What is cowpea (beans) called in Yoruba, Hausa and Igbo?

Cowpea (Beans) is called Ẹ̀wà (Yoruba), Wake (Hausa) and Agwa (Igbo).

When is cowpea (beans) harvested in Nigeria?

Cowpea (Beans) is usually harvested from September to November.

Which Nigerian states grow the most cowpea (beans)?

Kano, Borno, Katsina, Kaduna, Zamfara, Sokoto, Bauchi, Gombe, Yobe and Niger are among the best-known cowpea (beans) states.

Can I grow cowpea (beans) in my part of Nigeria?

Yes. Cowpea (Beans) grows in every region of Nigeria: North and South.

What diseases attack cowpea (beans) and how do I prevent them?

Maruca pod borer & flower thrips (pests): Spray recommended insecticide at flowering and podding, or grow PBR cowpea. Cowpea aphid-borne mosaic virus: Use resistant varieties and clean seed; control aphids early.
